text:
sarah_support: FYI we're getting a SEV escalation from Acme: persistent 502s and timeouts hitting /v1/generate for ~20m. Customers see 5xx + long tails. Support ticket: https://zendesk/acme/4521

elena_customer_success: They're on hosted. Errors started after a large batch import at 09:12 UTC. Seeing spikes in request latency before 5xx.

opsbot: Alert: redis-prefix-cache: error-rate 18% over 5m, avg latency 420ms, 50th 200ms. Node pool hotspot in eu-west-1.

sanjay_runtime: Can you paste a sample request id and raw headers from the logs? Need to trace routing and prefix lookup.

sarah_support: request_id: req_0a9f3b, raw log attached from gateway: "GET /v1/generate 504 upstream_timeout prefix_lookup failed"

kevin_oncall: Checking redis cluster status now, running `redis-cli -c CLUSTER INFO` and node `INFO`

kevin_oncall: Got intermittent MOVED replies and slow responses on keys with prefix `acct:acme:prompt_cache:` - looks like heavy fanout on prefix scans after import.

maya_infra: That fits - we rolled the new prefix-ttl optimization at 08:58; it added a background scan job to prime prefixes. Looks like the job created hot keys and exhausted connection pools causing prefix lookup timeouts.

sanjay_runtime: Repro steps from prod traces: client -> edge -> api-gateway -> prefix-cache lookup (redis) -> model router. When prefix lookup times out we bubble 502/504 from gateway.

kevin_oncall: Immediate mitigation: 1) scale redis prefix pool (x2 connections), 2) throttle background priming job, 3) route Acme's traffic to backup region. I've increased connection limits and paused the priming job.

opsbot: Change: priming-job paused by maya_infra at 09:36 UTC. Redis connection pool size increased from 200 -> 400 across prefix nodes.

elena_customer_success: I told Acme we're investigating and applied a mitigations note. They want ETA for full resolution.

maya_infra: Proposed fix: revert priming heuristic until we implement a sharded priming approach and per-tenant rate limiting on prefix scans. Also add fail-open semantics for prefix cache lookup after 200ms so we can serve behind a degraded cache.

sanjay_runtime: Agree. Follow-ups: 1) revert or throttle rollout flags for prefix-ttl optimization, 2) add circuit breaker in gateway to degrade to model routing without prefix lookup, 3) add additional metrics: per-tenant prefix QPS and prefix lookup latency P95.

kevin_oncall: I've rolled a canary that disables priming for top 20 tenants and connection pressure dropped. 5xx rate fell to baseline.

opsbot: Incident note created: INC-2391234567-redis-prefix-fanout. Postmortem owner: sanjay_runtime.

elena_customer_success: Acme confirmed reduced errors, asked for postmortem and SLA credit options.

sarah_support: Ticket updated, will escalate billing/SLA once postmortem is ready.

maya_infra: Action items assigned: sanjay_runtime - gateway circuit breaker + metrics; maya_infra - implement sharded priming + tenant rate limits; kevin_oncall - redis autoscaling playbook and safer priming flags.

kevin_oncall: Notes for runbook update: avoid priming tasks that fan out >100k keys per tenant; use incremental cursors and backoff.

sanjay_runtime: Quick repro snippet for engineers (do not run in prod):
```
# bad pattern: naive prefix scan
for key in redis.scan_iter(match="acct:acme:prompt_cache:*"):
    redis.mget(key)
```
Use SCAN with small COUNT and cursor, or maintain explicit prefix index.

kevin_oncall: I'll schedule a post-incident page and link relevant PRs once merged. Closing slack thread after postmortem draft. :white_check_mark:
